newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen Central Bank gives treasury bill results.
newsitem.headline: Yemen Central Bank gives treasury bill results.

text.p: The Central Bank of Yemen said on Saturday its latest issue of 91-day treasury bills yielded an average 17.95 percent, down on the average 19.02 percent at the April 8 auction.
Of the three billion rials worth of bills on offer, the issue attracted subscriptions worth 2.91 billion rials.
The average price was 9,571.67 rials and the lowest price accepted was 9,556.49 rials. Yields ranged from 18.61 percent to 12.41 percent.

The latest issue of 182-day bills yielded an average 18.21 percent, from 19.66 percent at the previous auction. Of the one billion rials worth of bills on offer, the issue attracted subscriptions worth 970 million rials.
The average price was 9,167.65 rials and the lowest price accepted was 9,154.60 rials. Yields ranged from 17.44 percent to 18.21 percent.
The latest issue of 364-day bills yielded an average 18.43 percent, against the April 8 average of 19.83 percent.
Of the 500 million rials worth of bills, the issue attracted subscriptions worth 485 million rials.
The average price was 8,447.31 rials and the lowest price accepted was 8,407.03 rials.
Yields ranged from 18 percent to 19 percent.
The bank did not fix a date for the next auction. One of its officials said recently the bank had "decided to hold the auction twice a week".
